title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Evaluating Responses - Responsiveness
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: During the evaluation of an IFB, it is discovered that the apparent lowest bidder failed to sign the official bid certification form. According to standard public procurement law, the buyer must:
options: Call the vendor to come in and sign it immediately
Reject the bid as non-responsive because a missing signature represents a failure to be legally bound to the offer
Waive the missing signature as a minor informality
Accept the bid but hold the vendor's bid bond until they sign
questions.explain: A signature on a bid form is a material requirement that legally binds the vendor to the terms and prices offered. Failure to sign renders the bid non-responsive and cannot be waived.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: In response to a sealed IFB, a vendor includes a cover letter stating that their price is valid only if the agency deletes the 'Liquidated Damages' clause. How must the buyer respond?
options: Accept the bid but ignore the letter
Reject the bid as non-responsive because the vendor took exception to material terms and conditions
Negotiate the clause since they are the lowest bidder
Forward the letter to the agency's legal counsel to redraft the contract
questions.explain: In an IFB, taking exception to material terms and conditions or attempting to impose counter-offers renders the bid conditionally qualified, which is legally non-responsive and must be rejected.
